1	# Arming the standing skills — the detail behind SKILL.md §1
2	
3	Run once, on invoke. SKILL.md carries the one-line summary of each; this is what
4	each one actually means.
5	
6	- **`tickets-zordon`** — read `TICKETS.md` at the repo root. Missing? Say so and
7	  create it on the first ticket, not before. Run its archive step first
8	  (`archive-tickets.sh`; moved rows → commit board + archive together), then
9	  report the open set: `B` bugs, `F` features, `A` agent-found.
10	- **`code-yoda`** — load it (an arm, not a direct invoke: no code-yoda banner); its core is the session's restraint level
11	  (`full` unless the user set another) and governs *what* gets built from here
12	  on. If `PONYTAIL MODE ACTIVE` is already in context, the external ponytail
13	  plugin has injected that same core and shows the level in its statusline
14	  badge: code-yoda's own §0 guard then skips the core, and only its three modes
15	  (review · audit · debt) are new. Report the level either way. A suggestion
16	  to run one of its modes, whenever you make one, is a single line in Yoda's
17	  voice, chosen from code-yoda §8 — "Heavy, this diff is. A review from
18	  code-yoda, take you should."
19	- **`codegraph`** — the code map the rest of the skill leans on. Check in order:
20	  `command -v codegraph` → missing? say so and offer
21	  `npm i -g @colbymchenry/codegraph` (never install silently). Present but
22	  `codegraph status` shows **0 files / 0 nodes** → `codegraph init` (then
23	  `codegraph index` if it was already initialized), **once**. Still 0 after that
24	  means the repo has no indexable source — a docs/skills/config repo — so say
25	  `codegraph: no code to index` and never retry it this session. Already indexed
26	  → `codegraph sync` (a stale index miscounts; status flags it as pending
27	  changes or an older engine).
28	  **Then count its coverage — codegraph is a map of some files, not the repo.**
29	  Compare `codegraph status` "Files" with `git ls-files | wc -l`, and read its
30	  "Files by Language". Report `codegraph <indexed>/<tracked> (<langs> only)`.
31	  It is **`codegraph: partial`** when indexed is under half of tracked, or the
32	  repo tracks any `.sh`, `.ps1` or `.md` (codegraph indexes none of them). On
33	  a partial map, codegraph answers only for js/ts/py symbols; every blast
34	  radius also runs `git grep -l` (ground-rules.md, "Map before you cut"). Measured on
35	  skillator2: 22/952 indexed, 0 of the 58 files that name `relay-morpheus.sh`
36	  found by codegraph, all 58 by `git grep -l relay-morpheus.sh`.
37	- **`live-friday`** — if the repo has a runnable surface (a dev script,
38	  `Cargo.toml`, `CMakeLists.txt`, a `Makefile`, `go.mod`, a Python entry point),
39	  it is armed: the *first* change to that project starts the app or build in the
40	  background and hands over the URL/command **before** the edits, so the user
41	  watches it run instead of waiting on a reply. Nothing runnable → say
42	  `live-friday: nothing to launch` once and drop it. Never auto-launch
43	  simulators, migrations or deploys.
44	- **`watch-cortana`** — on **Claude Code**, confirm the hooks are wired
45	  (`statusLine` runs `usage-watch … -Mode probe`, a `Stop` hook runs
46	  `-Mode gate`). Not wired → say so in one line and offer to wire it; never wire
47	  it silently. On **every other host** there is no hook that can read the usage %
48	and inject at turn end (cursor and antigravity have turn-end hooks; they have no
49	percentage to give them — see `PLATFORMS.md`), so run
50	  `usage-watch.ps1 -Mode check` / `usage-watch.sh check` once here and report
51	  exactly what it says. It reads a real percentage on codex and reports "no
52	  usage signal on this host" on cursor and antigravity — repeat that verbatim
53	  rather than calling it armed. See that skill's **Other hosts** table.
54	- **`rules-orko`** — run `sh <rules-orko>/scripts/rules-orko.sh show` (Windows:
55	  `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File
56	  "<rules-orko>/scripts/rules-orko.ps1" show`; `<rules-orko>` is that skill's
57	  directory, a sibling of this one). It prints the repo's committed rules
58	  (`.skillator/rules.md`) and this user's own (`~/.skillator/rules.md`),
59	  scope-tagged. Read both lists before the first task; every line binds the
60	  session as if the user had just typed it. A global rule contradicting a
61	  project rule is **asked** - one `AskUserQuestion` per clash, before the work
62	  it touches - never settled by you (`rules-orko/references/clashes.md`). Report
63	  the counts in the active-set line: `rules-orko: 2 project · 1 global`; both
64	  files absent → `rules-orko: none`. From here on, a standing rule the user
65	  states ("from now on", "always", "never", "in this repo") routes to
66	  `rules-orko` and is on disk before the next tool call.
67	- **`tiers`** (F39) — resolve tier → model for this host once per session, so
68	  `build-jarvis` never has to ask which model. Read `.skillator/tiers.local.md`:
69	  - missing, or its `host:` is not this host → write it: `deep`, `build` and
70	    `cheap` each set to the **first** slug in this host's column of
71	    `PLATFORMS.md` § Role tiers (Claude Code: `fable` / `opus` / `sonnet`, the
72	    Agent tool's `model` values; codex: `gpt-6-astra/high` / `gpt-6-astra/medium`
73	    / `gpt-6-astra/low`), a model the user named in this session winning over
74	    the column;
75	  - present → keep its models, drop every `down:` line not dated today.
76	  The shape (`host:`, `deep:`, `build:`, `cheap:`, `written:`, `down:` lines) is
77	  `skills/build-jarvis/references/grade.md` § The tiers file. The file is local to
78	  this machine and account: make sure the repo's `.gitignore` carries
79	  `.skillator/*.local.md` (append the line if missing; a repo with no
80	  `.gitignore` gets one with that line). Report `tiers deep=<m> build=<m>
81	  cheap=<m>`, plus `(<m> down)` for any model marked down today. Nothing is
82	  probed: a model that turns out unavailable is marked down by build-jarvis at
83	  dispatch, which retries one tier lower.
84	  On **Claude Code** also check that `build-jarvis`'s `UserPromptSubmit` route
85	  hook is wired (`build-jarvis/references/route-hook.md`); not wired → say so in
86	  one line and offer it, never wire it silently.
87	- **Upstream watch** (F23c, F29) — only in a repo that has
88	  `skills/design-arwen/UPSTREAM.md` (skillator itself); anywhere else skip it
89	  silently, because those tickets belong on skillator's board, not the user's.
90	  Run `sh practice/scripts/upstream-check.sh --daily` (Windows:
91	  `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File
92	  practice/scripts/upstream-check.ps1 -Daily`). `--daily` makes it a no-op after
93	  the first finished run of the day; the stamp is
94	  `$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/skillator/upstream-check.day`, shared by
95	  every worktree. Also run `sh skills/code-yoda/upstream-check.sh --daily`
96	  (Windows: the `.ps1` beside it, `-Daily`) — code-yoda's manifest, same
97	  output shape, its own stamp. Act on the output of both:
98	  - `skipped:` or exit 0: nothing to do.
99	  - each `changed <name> <old>..<new> <url>` line (exit 1, and also exit 2,
100	    because one failed row does not hide another's change): look for an open
101	    (`[ ]` or `[~]`) ticket line in `TICKETS.md` that names both `<name>` and
102	    `<new>`. If there is one, it is already logged. If not, take a number with
103	    `sh practice/scripts/next-id.sh A` and add
104	    `- [ ] A<n> — absorb <name> <old>..<new> into <skill> (<url>)`, `<skill>`
105	    being the one whose manifest reported it (`design-arwen`, or `code-yoda` for
106	    `ponytail`). The procedure is in that skill's `UPSTREAM.md`.
107	  - each `error` line (exit 2): report it in the active-set line as
108	    `upstreams: check failed (<name>)`. Never call a failed check unchanged. No
109	    stamp is written, so the next session retries it.
110	
111	  This is detection and a ticket, never an edit to the skill. Absorbing is a
112	  normal ticket that someone takes on purpose.
113	
114	Then state the active set in **one line** — not a feature tour:
115	
116	```
117	grayskull-power: board 3 open (B2, F7, A1) · codegraph 22/952 (js/py/ts only) · code-yoda full · live-friday armed (npm run dev) · watch-cortana armed at 92% · rules-orko: 2 project · 1 global · tiers deep=fable build=opus cheap=sonnet
118	```
119	
120	The banner is printed at the top of the reply, before any of this. It fires
121	**once per session**, on invoke — not on every routed request.
122	
123	---
124	
125	# Persist it for this project (once, then never again)
126	
127	Activation should survive the session and the host. Every one of these CLIs
128	already reads an always-on instruction file from the repo root — that is the
129	carrier, no hook required.
130	
131	On the **first** invoke in a repo, write these four small files and say so in
132	one line. If `.skillator/grayskull.md` already exists, activation is already
133	persisted: skip this whole step silently.
134	
135	**`.skillator/grayskull.md`** — the single source of truth:
136	
137	```markdown
138	# grayskull-power is ON for this project
139	
140	Load and follow `skillator:grayskull-power` for all work here, before
141	anything else. Claude Code: `Skill` tool; Antigravity: `/grayskull-power`;
142	Pi: `/skill:grayskull-power`; Codex/Cursor: read that skill's `SKILL.md`.
143	Print its banner once per session, then route per table.
144	
145	Standing rules:
146	- `TICKETS.md` is the board — `skillator:tickets-zordon` owns it.
147	- Reproduce before fixing; map with `codegraph` first.
148	- Before every commit: regression sweep, then `/code-review`
149	  (`code-review:code-review`) on the staged diff. `skillator:audit-sherlock`
150	  is the whole-app sweep — pre-release, handover, rot — never per-commit,
151	  never inside an implementer.
152	- Staged work runs to the end, no stop between stages. Six stops: a
153	  destructive op, a security-sensitive action, a side effect outside this
154	  worktree (merge, push, publish), the 7-day limit at 90%, a scope-contract
155	  breach, a failed repro. Else log a `Ruling:` in the run file.
156	  `skillator:relay-morpheus` owns `.skillator/run.md`, updated before
157	  dispatch, never after.
158	- One task per fresh implementer, own prompt, no session history —
159	  `skillator:tasks-sentinels` runs that loop. Same-file tasks do not fan out.
160	- Usage watch — before each non-trivial step run
161	  `<SKILL_DIR>/../watch-cortana/hooks/usage-watch.sh check`
162	  (Windows: `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File
163	  "<SKILL_DIR>/../watch-cortana/hooks/usage-watch.ps1" -Mode check`).
164	  It prints `HANDOFF NOW` plus an order — follow it. Claude Code's `Stop`
165	  hook does this already; skip it.
166	```
167	
168	Write that block **verbatim**, with exactly one substitution — `<SKILL_DIR>`,
169	which occurs twice (once for `.sh`, once for `.ps1`). Nothing else in the block
170	varies per repo.
171	
172	`<SKILL_DIR>` is the directory that contains grayskull-power's own `SKILL.md`:
173	
174	- **Normally** — the skill is installed outside the repo — write its **absolute**
175	  path, forward slashes, no trailing slash. e.g.
176	  `C:/Users/me/.claude/plugins/skillator/skills/grayskull-power`.
177	- **If that directory is inside the repo being activated** (skillator itself,
178	  dogfooding), write it **relative to the repo root** instead —
179	  `skills/grayskull-power` — so the file stays correct for every clone.
180	
181	Leave the `/../watch-cortana/…` tail exactly as written; do **not** pre-normalise
182	the `/../` away. The check at `practice/scripts/check-grayskull-sync.sh` compares
183	the live `.skillator/grayskull.md` against this block on precisely that rule, so
184	a hand-tidied path reads as drift.
185	
186	The path must resolve to a real `usage-watch.sh`. In any repo that is *not*
187	skillator, a repo-relative `skills/watch-cortana/…` does not exist — that is why
188	the absolute form is the default.
189	
190	Then the three host pointers, **appended** (never overwriting what is there):
191	
192	| File | Read by | Line to append |
193	|---|---|---|
194	| `CLAUDE.md` | Claude Code | `@.skillator/grayskull.md` |
195	| `AGENTS.md` | Codex, Cursor | `Read and follow ./.skillator/grayskull.md before any work in this repo.` |
196	| `GEMINI.md` | Antigravity | `@.skillator/grayskull.md` |
197	
198	Create a file only if it is missing; if it exists, append the line only when it
199	isn't already present. Three near-identical pointers is deliberate — each host
200	reads its own name, and a symlink is not portable to Windows.
201	
202	Deactivating is deleting `.skillator/grayskull.md`; the pointers then resolve to
203	nothing and are harmless. Say that once, don't repeat it.

  dispatch, which retries one tier lower.
  On **Claude Code** also check that `build-jarvis`'s `UserPromptSubmit` route
  hook is wired (`build-jarvis/references/route-hook.md`); not wired → say so in
  one line and offer it, never wire it silently.
- **Upstream watch** (F23c, F29) — only in a repo that has
  `skills/design-arwen/UPSTREAM.md` (skillator itself); anywhere else skip it
  silently, because those tickets belong on skillator's board, not the user's.
  Run `sh practice/scripts/upstream-check.sh --daily` (Windows:
  `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File
  practice/scripts/upstream-check.ps1 -Daily`). `--daily` makes it a no-op after
  the first finished run of the day; the stamp is
  `$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/skillator/upstream-check.day`, shared by
  every worktree. Also run `sh skills/code-yoda/upstream-check.sh --daily`
  (Windows: the `.ps1` beside it, `-Daily`) — code-yoda's manifest, same
  output shape, its own stamp. Act on the output of both:
  - `skipped:` or exit 0: nothing to do.
  - each `changed <name> <old>..<new> <url>` line (exit 1, and also exit 2,
    because one failed row does not hide another's change): look for an open
    (`[ ]` or `[~]`) ticket line in `TICKETS.md` that names both `<name>` and
    `<new>`. If there is one, it is already logged. If not, take a number with
    `sh practice/scripts/next-id.sh A` and add
    `- [ ] A<n> — absorb <name> <old>..<new> into <skill> (<url>)`, `<skill>`
    being the one whose manifest reported it (`design-arwen`, or `code-yoda` for
    `ponytail`). The procedure is in that skill's `UPSTREAM.md`.
  - each `error` line (exit 2): report it in the active-set line as
    `upstreams: check failed (<name>)`. Never call a failed check unchanged. No
    stamp is written, so the next session retries it.

  This is detection and a ticket, never an edit to the skill. Absorbing is a
  normal ticket that someone takes on purpose.

Then state the active set in **one line** — not a feature tour:

```

```

The banner is printed at the top of the reply, before any of this. It fires
**once per session**, on invoke — not on every routed request.

---

# Persist it for this project (once, then never again)

Activation should survive the session and the host. Every one of these CLIs
already reads an always-on instruction file from the repo root — that is the
carrier, no hook required.

On the **first** invoke in a repo, write these four small files and say so in
one line. If `.skillator/grayskull.md` already exists, activation is already
persisted: skip this whole step silently.

**`.skillator/grayskull.md`** — the single source of truth:

```markdown
# grayskull-power is ON for this project

Load and follow `skillator:grayskull-power` for all work here, before
anything else. Claude Code: `Skill` tool; Antigravity: `/grayskull-power`;
Pi: `/skill:grayskull-power`; Codex/Cursor: read that skill's `SKILL.md`.
Print its banner once per session, then route per table.

Standing rules:
- `TICKETS.md` is the board — `skillator:tickets-zordon` owns it.
- Reproduce before fixing; map with `codegraph` first.
- Before every commit: regression sweep, then `/code-review`
  (`code-review:code-review`) on the staged diff. `skillator:audit-sherlock`
  is the whole-app sweep — pre-release, handover, rot — never per-commit,
  never inside an implementer.
- Staged work runs to the end, no stop between stages. Six stops: a
  destructive op, a security-sensitive action, a side effect outside this
  worktree (merge, push, publish), the 7-day limit at 90%, a scope-contract
  breach, a failed repro. Else log a `Ruling:` in the run file.
  `skillator:relay-morpheus` owns `.skillator/run.md`, updated before
  dispatch, never after.
- One task per fresh implementer, own prompt, no session history —
  `skillator:tasks-sentinels` runs that loop. Same-file tasks do not fan out.
- Usage watch — before each non-trivial step run
  `<SKILL_DIR>/../watch-cortana/hooks/usage-watch.sh check`
  (Windows: `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File
  "<SKILL_DIR>/../watch-cortana/hooks/usage-watch.ps1" -Mode check`).
  It prints `HANDOFF NOW` plus an order — follow it. Claude Code's `Stop`
  hook does this already; skip it.
```

Write that block **verbatim**, with exactly one substitution — `<SKILL_DIR>`,
which occurs twice (once for `.sh`, once for `.ps1`). Nothing else in the block
varies per repo.

`<SKILL_DIR>` is the directory that contains grayskull-power's own `SKILL.md`:

- **Normally** — the skill is installed outside the repo — write its **absolute**
  path, forward slashes, no trailing slash. e.g.
  `C:/Users/me/.claude/plugins/skillator/skills/grayskull-power`.
- **If that directory is inside the repo being activated** (skillator itself,
  dogfooding), write it **relative to the repo root** instead —
  `skills/grayskull-power` — so the file stays correct for every clone.

Leave the `/../watch-cortana/…` tail exactly as written; do **not** pre-normalise
the `/../` away. The check at `practice/scripts/check-grayskull-sync.sh` compares
the live `.skillator/grayskull.md` against this block on precisely that rule, so
a hand-tidied path reads as drift.

The path must resolve to a real `usage-watch.sh`. In any repo that is *not*
skillator, a repo-relative `skills/watch-cortana/…` does not exist — that is why
the absolute form is the default.

Then the three host pointers, **appended** (never overwriting what is there):

| File | Read by | Line to append |
|---|---|---|
| `CLAUDE.md` | Claude Code | `@.skillator/grayskull.md` |
| `AGENTS.md` | Codex, Cursor | `Read and follow ./.skillator/grayskull.md before any work in this repo.` |
| `GEMINI.md` | Antigravity | `@.skillator/grayskull.md` |

Create a file only if it is missing; if it exists, append the line only when it
isn't already present. Three near-identical pointers is deliberate — each host
reads its own name, and a symlink is not portable to Windows.

Deactivating is deleting `.skillator/grayskull.md`; the pointers then resolve to
nothing and are harmless. Say that once, don't repeat it.
